content: As the industry navigates increasingly complex operational environments, the demand for sophisticated IT services is growing exponentially, fundamentally driven by the sector's pressing need for comprehensive modernization and stringent regulatory compliance. The foundational trajectory of this digital shift has been documented over several years of industry evolution. As highlighted by the adoption trends within the sector, the growing demand for IT services is fundamentally driven by sector-specific needs aimed at modernization and strict regulatory compliance. As mining firms face increasing pressure from both local authorities and international stakeholders to adhere to stringent environmental, social, and governance regulations, the deployment of advanced IT solutions becomes indispensable for accurate reporting, real-time monitoring, and compliance verification. These regulatory and procedural standards form the foundation for positioning and compliance within the context of IT services contracts. Although IT services are distinct from traditional construction, they frequently intersect with public infrastructure projects, necessitating a thorough comprehension of specialized grading and registration protocols. Understanding these requirements is critical for vendor compliance. According to comprehensive guidelines available as of June 2026, general registration on the Central Supplier Database requires a standard set of essential documentation [65] . These baseline prerequisites, which are applicable to all suppliers including those in the IT sector, include company registration certificates such as the CoR14.3, identification documents for company directors, verifiable proof of business address, a valid tax clearance certificate, and the acquisition of a unique supplier number. Meeting these standard registration obligations is non-negotiable for firms seeking to secure public sector IT contracts. While the operational framework of the Central Supplier Database remains constant over time, specific regulations concerning IT vendors could evolve, illustrating the critical importance of verifying requirements directly through the official database or related government publications [63] .
